title: Adding a 2nd M.2 Slot to a Lenovo M710q Tiny
summary: Hand-soldered the unpopulated second M.2 NVMe/SATA slot on my homelab server's motherboard.

blocks.caption: The new SSD2 slot, recognized and running

blocks.html:
My Lenovo ThinkCentre M710q has been the backbone of my homelab, and it was running out of storage.

Instead of just buying a larger drive, I took the DIY route: populate the unpopulated second M.2 slot on the motherboard. After digging through community guides, I ordered the M.2 connector and supporting components from LCSC, fired up the soldering iron and got to work.

After careful hand-soldering and fixing a few minor solder bridges, the board recognized a spare 120GB M.2 SATA SSD.

blocks.caption: M.2 connector fitted to the empty pads

blocks.html:
CPU: upgraded from the stock i5-7500 to a salvaged Core i7-7700, with a 90W adapter for the extra TDP
RAM: 16GB (2 × 8GB) DDR4
Storage: 256GB NVMe + 250GB 2.5" SATA SSD in a mirrored RAID for OS and critical data, plus the new 120GB M.2 SATA SSD
Services: Proxmox running Ubuntu Server, Home Assistant and TrueNAS
There is something very satisfying about making unpopulated motherboard pads actually work. Thanks to the homelab and hardware communities for the documentation and inspiration.

title: Home Assistant Aquarium Controller
summary: Custom PCB that monitors the aquarium and automates the filter pump and plant lighting via Home Assistant.

blocks.caption: Hand-soldered 0603 components on the custom PCB

blocks.html:
A custom controller for our home aquarium. It integrates with Home Assistant to monitor the tank, automate the filter pump and run the lighting schedule for the plants.

My wife and I designed the PCB together, and she hand-soldered most of the SMT parts (mostly 0603). She has been a huge part of keeping me going on this embedded journey.

blocks.caption: Assembly under the microscope in the home lab

blocks.html:
With every new design I make mistakes. Usually I can fix them; occasionally one is unfixable. Even with checking and double-checking, it happens, though less often now.

Many new hardware designers get frustrated when they find a mistake after the PCBA has already arrived. Don't. Take a deep breath, gather your rework tools and fix as much as you can, then learn from it for the next revision.

title: BLE Passive Keyless Entry for Mobility Vehicles
summary: STM32 + BLE walk-away lock / approach unlock with phone-controlled ignition.

blocks.caption: Inside the unit: BLE module and relay board

blocks.html: Firmware for a BLE-based Passive Keyless Entry (PKE) device for mobility vehicles, completed over an Eid break. The goal: a seamless, secure and responsive walk-away lock / approach unlock experience, controlled entirely from a smartphone.

MCU: STM32 family, for processing power and low-power efficiency
Communication: W02 BLE module for proximity sensing and data transmission
Firmware: custom state machine handling security handshakes and relay logic, keeping the vehicle secure even in noisy RF environments

Proximity-based auto unlock / lock
Remote ignition control from a custom mobile app (NOJOR)
Real-time battery voltage monitoring

There is something very satisfying about code on a screen turning into a physical relay click that powers a vehicle. Next step: refining the proximity algorithms. App development was a collaboration with MD Ahsan Hasib.

title: Porting ArduPilot to a Custom Flight Controller
summary: Weekend project bringing up ArduPilot (ChibiOS) on custom flight-controller hardware.

blocks.html: A weekend learning project: porting ArduPilot to a custom flight controller. Along the way it became clear that ChibiOS, the RTOS inside ArduPilot, is an excellent learning resource for anyone getting into embedded firmware engineering. It is real, production-grade code.

blocks.text: Why it's great for new embedded engineers

blocks.html:
Clean, well-structured peripheral drivers (UART, SPI, I²C, ADC, DMA)
A proper hardware abstraction layer for multi-MCU support
Real-time task scheduling done right
Sensor handling with strict timing constraints
Proven, stable code running on real flying systems

Unlike simple demo projects, this stack shows how professional embedded firmware is actually written, from board bring-up to real-time execution. If you want to move beyond blinking LEDs, exploring ArduPilot's ChibiOS implementation is one of the best hands-on paths available.

title: Universal VTS Telematics Device
summary: Designed and manufactured in Bangladesh: one GPS/OBD2 tracker speaking GT06, Teltonika and H02 protocols.

blocks.caption: GNSS, cellular and backup battery inside the IP67 enclosure

blocks.html: Two friends and I started brainstorming how we could contribute to Bangladesh with our embedded engineering expertise. One idea stood out: the Vehicle Tracking System (VTS) market. Over 60 importers in Bangladesh source VTS devices from nearly 40 suppliers worldwide, yet there was still a gap for a reliable product at a competitive price.

Instant alerts when someone touches the car
Accurate mileage tracking for every trip
Fuel consumption data and route analytics for fleets
Real-time location and door status for private owners
Geofencing to manage misuse
Freezer-van temperature monitoring for food and pharma suppliers

So we built one standardized, adaptable device for most of these use cases: a universal telematics device that supports multiple protocols (GT06, GT06F, Teltonika, H02) in one unit, so it connects to existing service providers' platforms.

GNSS + AGPS for fast, accurate positioning
Real-time GPS + OBD2 diagnostics
Smart alerts
Sensor-ready: fuel, temperature, door and more
Rugged IP67 enclosure, long battery backup, high-gain GPS antenna
Smart power management to protect the vehicle battery while staying connected 24/7
After rounds of prototyping, we are now manufacturing our own VTS devices in-house for customers. Designed, developed and built in Bangladesh, for the world.

title: BiTOn: Smart EV Charger (EVSE)
summary: 6–32A adjustable EV charger with solar load balancing, GFCI, app control and Wi-Fi/BLE/GSM.

blocks.html: BiTOn is my EVSE (electric vehicle supply equipment) project. Sustainable transportation is the future, and this is my part in it.

Adjustable charging current from 6A to 32A: lower it to run only on excess solar, or raise it to charge faster from the grid
Power monitoring and dynamic load balancing for solar or battery storage
Phase upgradeable: single-phase now, with a path to 3-phase Level 2
Safety: GFCI ground-fault detection at 30mA AC leakage
Protection: over-current, over-voltage and under-voltage
Connectivity: Wi-Fi, BLE 4.2 and 2G/3G GSM for server communication and SMS alerts
Smartphone app for remote monitoring and control
Temperature monitoring of the magnetic contactor
OTA updates

Display: PCD8544 (the Nokia 5110 LCD), for a touch of nostalgia
Metering: PZEM-004T for voltage, current and power. Not EVSE-class, but fine for the MVP; version one moves to a DIN-rail RS485 energy meter, and later an on-board meter
Switching: an SSR drives the magnetic contactor that switches the 32A load
Brain: ESP32 LilyGO T-Call SIM800 for the MVP; planned move to an ESP32-WROVER with a PCIe GSM modem
Thanks to Abul Hasnat for guiding me on this journey from an early age.

title: Smart Cane
summary: Ultrasonic-based smart cane that helps visually impaired users detect obstacles and navigate safely.

blocks.html: Visually challenged persons face great difficulty in independent mobility and use the white cane as a mobility aid to detect close-by obstacles on the ground. However, the cane has many limitations. It can only detect obstacles up to knee level. Hence, the user cannot detect raised obstacles like elevated bars and frequently collides with them. Another problem is that the cane can only detect obstacles within 1 meter from the user. Also, obstacles like moving vehicles cannot be detected until dangerously close to the person. There is no smart cane available for automatic navigation to guide a person in outdoor navigation independently in urban areas, regardless of the person’s hearing status for reaching a particular destination. Based in WHO report (2011), 15% of our population is disabled and among them more than 4 million people are visual impaired. Almost 90% of the blind persons live in developing countries, with a majority below poverty line and hi-tech products are unaffordable to them. Access to such a smart cane is not available for individuals who are blind.

According to researchers, 83% of the physical input data from environment come through “Eyes”. Nearly 4 million of world’s population is blind, and hence deprived of one of the most important and informative asset “Eyes”. People with complete blindness or low vision often have a difficult time self-navigating outside well-known environments. In fact, physical movement is one of the biggest challenges for blind people. Traveling or simply walking down a crowded street may create great difficulty. Because of this, many people with low vision will bring a sighted friend, family member or walking cane to help navigate unknown environments. To make them independent we are proposing ultra-modern smart cane. We noticed that normal blind canes used by blinds have certain limitations like detecting pot-holes, detect objects, above knee obstacles etc. at the same time currently available sensor equipped canes are very costly and unaffordable. We want to develop an economical sensor equipped cane capable of assisting blind to navigate easily via vibratory and auditory signals so that their regular movement will become more secure. There will be no chance to get collide with any obstacle. There will be no dependency. They can do their regular work without any help. They can go to shop, office, refreshing walk, education etc.

title: University Final Year Thesis
summary: Final year thesis on optimal MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit) sizing for network performance.

blocks.html: Maximum MTU (Maximum Transmission Unite) Calculation for any link

We mainly analyzes the impact of the maximum transmission unit (MTU) on application performance. Simulation models are created and amount of experiments for typical FTP applications are conducted. Based on comparisons with different MTU value and different scenarios corresponding to the FTP upload response time, optimal settings are found. Optimal settings are required to achieve minimal delay in a network. We have studied and analyzed possible reasons for causing network delays. We have obtained theoretical explanation and basic formulas to understand basic mechanism of fragmentation, packet switching, header calculation, multiple delay calculations (like queuing delay, propagation delay, processing delay, and transmission delay). From those theoretical expressions, we found parameters like link capacity, number of hops, number of headers, header sizes, packet sizes, fragmentation, etc. we have varied these parameters to MATLAB based simulations and tried to determine the theoretical concept. We have experimented multiple times varying parameter and given best output results.
